record.title: Controlled experiments report answer-prior bias across eight dense retrievers
record.summary: A Nov 8 arXiv paper reports that, across eight dense retrievers, a model's preference for a canonical answer predicts higher retrieval scores for passages containing that answer. In controlled LAMA/TREx template contrasts, this relationship also appears when the answer-matching passage expresses the wrong relation. The authors report positive correlations in both settings; their selected examples are single-token cases where the diagnostic already favors the canonical object. The study does not measure prevalence in natural corpora or downstream RAG outcomes.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report positive correlations between their answer-knowledge diagnostic and retrieval-score differences across eight dense retrievers in both object-contrast and relation–object-conflict template settings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the relation–object-conflict setting, the authors report that passages containing the canonical answer but expressing a different relation can receive higher retrieval scores than passages matching the relation but containing an alternative object.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish how often answer-prior bias occurs in natural corpora, its prevalence across ordinary factual queries, or its effect on downstream RAG task outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported correlations and retrieval preferences have not been independently recomputed in this activation.
The paper does not estimate prevalence or magnitude on natural passages, multi-token answers, temporal questions or production RAG tasks.

brief.importance_rationale: If the controlled effect transfers, retrieval systems may select familiar answer entities over relation-matching evidence, changing RAG evaluation and design choices. The current paper is a bounded, controlled study without natural-corpus prevalence or downstream impact measurements.
limitations: The passages are template-generated and do not capture the length, noise, entity interactions, or multiple relations of natural corpora.
Examples are limited to single-token answer pairs for which the diagnostic favors the canonical answer, then sampled conditionally; rates are not population estimates.
The alternative object in the main LAMA/TREx contrast is type-compatible but not asserted to be a true alternative fact for the subject; multiple valid answers are tested separately on QAMPARI.
No independent reproduction or downstream RAG outcome evaluation was performed here.
brief.summary: A Nov 8 arXiv paper reports that, across eight dense retrievers, a model's preference for a canonical answer predicts higher retrieval scores for passages containing that answer. In controlled LAMA/TREx template contrasts, this relationship also appears when the answer-matching passage expresses the wrong relation. The authors report positive correlations in both settings; their selected examples are single-token cases where the diagnostic already favors the canonical object. The study does not measure prevalence in natural corpora or downstream RAG outcomes.

technical.claimed_result: Across eight dense retrievers, object-knowledge diagnostic scores positively correlate with retrieval preferences in controlled template passages: r=.21–.52 in object-contrast and r=.13–.30 in relation–object conflict.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary preprint reports these controlled results. This activation did not independently reproduce them; no natural-corpus prevalence or downstream RAG effect was measured.
technical.mechanism: The authors hypothesize that a retriever's language-model answer preference affects passage ranking, sometimes outweighing relation match. Their diagnostic measures token-level preference for a canonical object over a type-compatible alternative.
technical.regime: LAMA/TREx factual triples converted into single-template passages; eight retrievers; one thousand sampled single-token examples per model, selected from examples where the canonical answer received the higher diagnostic score.
technical.reproducibility: Paper HTML is accessible. No independent reproduction was performed in this activation. Natural-corpus tests, broader multi-token coverage, and downstream RAG evaluation remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-pair contrasts hold query and relation fixed while changing answer object; relation–object-conflict contrasts compare an answer-matching wrong-relation passage against a relation-matching alternative-answer passage.

brief.title: Controlled experiments report answer-prior bias across eight dense retrievers
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported effect transfers beyond controlled passages, dense retrieval may favor familiar or stale answers over evidence that matches the requested relation, which matters for evidence selection in RAG. The present results justify testing this failure mode, not assuming it occurs at the same rate in natural retrieval.
